claims.text: The Australian government decided to withdraw 24 expeditioners from its Macquarie Island research station due to psychosocial risks posed by an expected H5 avian influenza mortality event.
A common dolphin found near Goolwa in South Australia tested positive for H5 bird flu, marking the second native mammal species in Australia confirmed to have contracted the virus.
Oil prices rose following reports that US President Donald Trump rejected re-establishing the terms of a June memorandum of understanding between the US and Iran.
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced Operation Economic Outcast sanctions targeting nearly 60 Iran-linked individuals, entities, and vessels to pressure Iran amid war with the US.
Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, warned that if the US blockade continues, Iran will target US economic interests 100 percent, with intensity and force.

Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei stated that Iran has the legitimate right to target the origin of any act of aggression, pointing specifically to US refueling aircraft departing from Bulgaria.
Qatari Prime Minister Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani met Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian in Tehran to discuss regional security and conditions for dialogue.
Mohsen Rezaei stated that Iran exported 80 million barrels of oil during the ceasefire period.
Mohsen Rezaei announced that Iran is drawing up a list of conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz after mediators asked Tehran to set out its terms.
Under a June Memorandum of Understanding, Iran agreed to clear mines and permit free vessel passage in the Strait of Hormuz for 60 days while the US agreed to lift its blockade and ease sanctions.
US President Donald Trump declared in the Oval Office that US forces had cleared mines from the Strait of Hormuz and that the waterway was open.
US President Donald Trump told Al Jazeera that he has no time schedule for negotiations with Iran and is in no hurry to resume talks.

US defence and NATO officials stated that the US military faces a critical shortage of Patriot missile interceptors in Europe due to interceptor stocks being redeployed to the Middle East for the war with Iran.
The Wall Street Journal reported that CIA Director John Ratcliffe traveled to Moscow to warn Russia not to attack NATO countries.
US President Donald Trump signed an executive order directing the Department of the Interior to rename Lake Ontario as Lake America.
The US Geological Survey updated the name of Lake Ontario to Lake America in its Geographic Names Information System following President Trump's order.
US President Donald Trump posted an altered 1948 Life magazine presidential ranking graphic on social media, placing himself at the top under a newly added category named greatest.

US President Donald Trump previously issued an executive order renaming the Gulf of Mexico as the Gulf of America, leading to a legal dispute with Mexico and an ongoing lawsuit by the Associated Press.
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney stated in a social media post that Canadians know things must be called by their name and that the lake is called Lake Ontario today and forever.
Democratic Representative Debbie Dingell of Michigan announced plans to introduce legislation in Congress to nullify President Trump's order renaming Lake Ontario.
Canadian US trade minister Dominic LeBlanc stated on X that the US had withdrawn demands regarding French language labelling requirements.
The US imposed 50% tariffs on $20 billion worth of Canadian goods following the collapse of trade negotiations between Washington and Ottawa.
The name Lake Ontario originates from the Huron Indigenous word oniatari:io, meaning lake of shining waters.
Lake Ontario lies along the international border separating the US state of New York from the Canadian province of Ontario.
Abrham Meareg filed a lawsuit in Kenya in 2022 alleging that Facebook's algorithm promoted posts calling for the murder of his father during northern Ethiopia's civil war.
Meta settled a lawsuit brought by 29 US states accusing it of designing addictive products for young people, agreeing to pay $18 billion and alter platform features in the US.
Meta agreed to pay $16.68 billion to settle claims from 29 US states alleging it designed its apps to addict teenagers and improperly harvested children's data.
In 2025, Meta's family of apps segment generated $198.8 billion in revenue and $102.5 billion in operating profit.
Instagram's user reach in India reached 481 million people in 2025, while Facebook's reach stood at 403 million.
Meta agreed to pay up to $17 billion in penalties to settle a landmark federal child safety lawsuit brought by California, Colorado, Kentucky, and New Jersey.

As part of its proposed settlement, Meta agreed to implement a default two-hour daily time limit for users under 18, a default block on nighttime use, and a ban on displaying like and reaction counts.
A glacier collapse in Nepal and Tibet triggered flash floods that killed at least 270 people and left more than 1,500 missing, including at least 65 Americans.
Meta reached a settlement agreement covering 47 states and several territories for up to $17.1 billion in penalties, alongside a separate $1 billion settlement in Texas.
Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers approved Meta's multi-state settlement agreement in federal court in Oakland, California.
British minister Pat McFadden stated that the UK government does not want a situation where children in the US receive a higher level of protection than children in the UK.
